clue.text: It carries documents for a murder trial maybe

parts.note: to despatch someone is to kill them, so murder means despatch
a court case is an example of a trial, hence 'maybe'

explanation.surface: A briefcase full of evidence being carried into a murder trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A despatch case is a flat leather briefcase for carrying official papers.

clue.text: Was half asleep when Edward held up raised sword

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word sword is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ED is the short form of Edward; in a down entry it sits at the bottom, holding up the piece above it

explanation.surface: A drowsy man named Edward, nodding off, holds a sword aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SWORD into DROWS; in the down entry ED then sits beneath it, holding it up, so 'held up' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To drowse is to doze, lingering between sleeping and waking.

clue.text: Its family must be the pride of the Pacific

definitions.text: Its family must be the pride of the Pacific

parts.words: Its family must be the pride of the Pacific
parts.note: a group of lions is called a pride, so a whimsical family of lions living in the ocean would be the pride of that ocean

explanation.surface: Some family is the boast of the Pacific region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' seems to mean glory, but it is the collective noun for lions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea lions are eared seals common along Pacific coasts, playfully treated as ocean-going lions.

clue.text: Impose condition to reinforce the cavalry troop

definitions.meaning: to attach an extra clause or proviso to a bill or agreement
read literally, to supply one more horseman to the mounted soldiers

explanation.definitionFit: A rider is both an added clause in a document and a horseman, so adding one either qualifies an agreement or strengthens a cavalry unit.

clue.text: Trophy I had as the love match victor

parts.note: a cup is a trophy given to a winner
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A tennis champion holds up the trophy after a love-game win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love match' suggests tennis scoring, but the victor in matters of love is the Roman god.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid, Roman god of desire, triumphs whenever lovers are paired off.

clue.text: RAF chef disposed to haggle

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged or set out, so the letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: An air force cook is inclined to bargain over prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaffer is an old word for bargaining or haggling over terms.

clue.text: Weather outlook is good for the scheduled fete

parts.note: something set is fixed or scheduled in advance
a fair is an outdoor fete or fair-day event

explanation.surface: The forecast is sunny for the planned village fete.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Set fair' is the barometer reading forecasting settled, fine weather.

clue.text: It supplies live wires for a current advertisement

parts.note: electric current, hence current suggests electric
a plug is a piece of publicity, a quick advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone energetic promotes a topical advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live wires' looks like lively people, but here it is literal: wires carrying power.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug connects an appliance's cable to the mains, feeding power to its conductors.

clue.text: What was spotted in the game-hunter's sights?

definitions.text: What was spotted in the game-hunter's sights?

parts.words: What was spotted in the game-hunter's sights?
parts.note: a big cat with a spotted coat seen through a hunter's rifle sights; 'spotted' means both seen and covered in spots

explanation.surface: A safari hunter asks what was seen through the rifle scope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as seen, but also describes the animal's markings.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat with a rosette-spotted coat is classic big-game quarry.

clue.text: Spectre appears softly before a month is out

indicators.note: before places the soft marking ahead of the following letters

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking meaning softly

indicators.note: out in the sense of disordered or wrong, so the letters of a month are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ghost quietly shows up shortly before a month ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' rearranges A MONTH into HANTOM, which follows P.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a ghost or apparition, the same as a spectre.

clue.text: Overlook full stop, and fail to see the argument

definitions.meaning: literally, fail to notice a punctuation mark ending a sentence, a point
not grasp the essential issue being made

explanation.definitionFit: A point is both a full stop and the crux of an argument, so missing one is literal or figurative misunderstanding.

clue.text: Take commission from a money collector

definitions.meaning: to strip an officer of rank, removing his military commission
someone handling cash at a bank or shop till

explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to dismiss an officer in disgrace; a cashier is also the bank or till clerk taking payments.

clue.text: Licks, having feasted riotously

indicators.note: riotously means wildly and in disorder, so the letters of feasted are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone wins by eating wildly at a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: To lick an opponent is informal for beating them soundly.

clue.text: Sounds of city being bombarded-with radioactive gas

indicators.note: the noise a word makes when spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a city under air attack has a raid on it: 'raid on'

explanation.surface: The noise of a city under bombardment, with poison gas in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed hyphen in 'bombarded-with' is a typesetting slip for a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is the radioactive noble gas produced by decaying uranium.

clue.text: Did Rommel hope he would run away and turn traitor?

definitions.text: Did Rommel hope he would run away and turn traitor?

parts.note: to desert is to abandon your post and flee
to rat is to betray or inform on your side

explanation.surface: A question about what the German commander wished of his enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rommel led the Afrika Korps in North Africa; the British 7th Armoured Division who faced him were nicknamed after a jerboa, a small burrowing animal of the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Rommel's opponents in the desert war were famously named for that rodent, so he would want them to flee and defect.

clue.text: A bleary eyed drunk is likely to visit his alter ego

definitions.text: A bleary eyed drunk is likely to
definitions.meaning: blurred vision from drink makes everything appear twice
literally, go to see his twin or doppelganger

explanation.definitionFit: Drunken blurred sight shows two of everything, and to call on one's alter ego is to see one's double.

clue.text: Orchestra suited to slow movement rather than a gallop

definitions.text: Orchestra suited to slow movement rather than a gallop

indicators.note: a movement implies the letters of Orchestra being shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: An orchestra suits a slow movement of a symphony better than a galloping tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks musical, the section of a symphony, but it rearranges ORCHESTRA; the whole clue then describes a heavy draught animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy draught animal bred for pulling loads plods rather than races.

clue.text: Footballers yell and dash from the stadium

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, a code of football, standing for its players
shout means yell

explanation.surface: Supporters bellow and hurry out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is Rugby Union, one of Britain's football codes.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave in haste is to hurry or charge out of somewhere.

clue.text: Cheer up and listen to a couple of quintets

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
two groups of five make ten

explanation.surface: Cheer yourself by listening to two five-piece bands.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage someone is to lift their spirits or embolden them.

clue.text: Situation a cautious punter may bet on

definitions.text: a cautious punter may bet on
definitions.meaning: a racing bet that pays if the horse finishes in the first few, rather than winning outright

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a position or spot and the each-way racing bet on finishing second or third.

clue.text: Nice crepes I served up

indicators.note: food served up is prepared and arranged, so the letters of crepes I are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pancakes made in the French city of Nice, dished up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' wants to be the French city, given the crepes, but it is the adjective meaning exact; 'served up' rearranges CREPES I.
explanation.definitionFit: A nice distinction is a fine, exact one, so nice can mean accurate.

clue.text: Formic queen. That's hard

parts.note: a queen insect is the mother of the colony, a dam: 'a dam'
formic means relating to ants, so it points to an ant

explanation.surface: A remark about the queen of an ant nest being tough.
explanation.walkthrough: A dam is a mother animal, and the queen is the mother of her colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant was once a legendary unbreakable substance, so the word means hard or unyielding.

clue.text: Grand Finale to a legislative programme

definitions.meaning: the closing section of a play or show
the final statute passed in a session of parliament

explanation.definitionFit: A play's final scenes are its closing part, and the final statute in a programme of laws is its closing one too.

clue.text: Pack of cards in which Jack has to be turned up

parts.note: jack and tar are both slang for a sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word to is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A deck of cards in which the knave must be face up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be turned up' makes TO into OT beneath TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot is a deck of picture cards used in fortune-telling and old card games.

clue.text: Herb adds nothing to orange squash

indicators.note: squash means crush out of shape, so the letters of orange are rearranged

parts.note: O, the round zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A herb is mixed into an orange drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' looks like the British fruit drink, but it is the anagram signal; 'adds nothing to' puts the round letter for zero at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is the aromatic herb widely used in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Unfair advantage for one finishing off the tiling

definitions.meaning: Australian slang, as in coming in on the ..., getting an unfair advantage
someone who fills the gaps between tiles with grout

explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang uses the word for an unearned edge, and literally it names whoever applies grout between tiles.

clue.text: Anglo-Celts should bear it in mind

indicators.note: in places the small word inside the word for mind

parts.note: brain means mind
taken as written

explanation.surface: People of English and Celtic descent should remember this.
explanation.definitionFit: The island nation is home to English, Scots, Welsh and other peoples of Anglo-Saxon and Celtic stock.

clue.text: Get up before taking driving exam and pass with flying colours

parts.note: to stand is to get up
a driving exam in Britain is called the test

explanation.surface: Rise early, take the driving test and sail through it.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove sound under examination is to survive trial and come through well.
